title: Wave3 scholarly-transcription mining: Shoju 120-122
purpose: Start a new source-expansion lane from Yamauchi's visible poem-specific transcription after v1.11 identified source coverage rather than operation invention as the main bottleneck.

shared_B_review.reason: Raw B=たま equality alone does not establish the same lexical/morphological boundary, and the tentative 賀・長寿 scene differs from shoju-031's 露/秋 context.

summary.research_conclusion: Wave3 source expansion can add real strict-palindrome evidence without immediately creating a safe crossover family. Candidate 121 is factor-isolated; candidate 122 has only a raw-B cross-scene contact that is intentionally not promoted.

safety_rules: Do not repair poem 120 to 31 kana by palindrome expectation.
A standard reading of an explicit kanji in scholarly transcription is recorded as a reading assumption, not as original-source furigana evidence.
Wave3 candidates remain separate from fixed50 and wave2 snapshots.
Raw factor equality does not create a transferable seam.
next_action: Continue wave3 mining for additional strict 31-kana poems, prioritizing records that create narrow-scene repeated A/E-operation lanes rather than merely increasing corpus count.
